title_options: Why Mosquitoes Bite You More Than Your Friends 🦟

share.myth: Mosquitoes pick people with sweet blood (or a certain blood type).
share.truth: In De Obaldia et al. 2022 (Cell), the people mosquitoes preferred had more carboxylic acids from skin oil on their skin, and the preference held for years; blood-type evidence is contradictory.
share.line: Mosquitoes don't choose sweet blood. They follow the smell of acids made from the oil on your skin.

facts: De Obaldia ME et al. 2022, Cell 185:4099: volunteers wore nylon sleeves on their forearms for 6 hours; female Aedes aegypti chose between pairs of nylons.

Subject 33's attractiveness score was over 100 times that of the two least attractive subjects (19 and 28); differences were stable over several years (Subject 28 least attractive of all 64 subjects).
Highly attractive people had significantly more carboxylic acids in their skin emanations; human sebum is about 25% free fatty acids.
Mutant mosquitoes lacking the co-receptors Ir8a, Ir25a or Ir76b were severely impaired but still told highly and weakly attractive people apart.
The paper notes evidence on ABO blood type and mosquito attraction is contradictory. Only females bite: they need blood protein to make eggs.
description: Some people really are mosquito magnets, and it's not sweet blood. A 2022 study traced it to acids made from the oil on their skin. #shorts #science #biology #mosquito
sources: De Obaldia et al. 2022, Cell 185:4099-4116 (skin carboxylic acids and mosquito attraction), open access via Europe PMC PMC10069481.

scenes.narration: Some people really are mosquito magnets. And it has nothing to do with sweet blood.
In one study, volunteers wore nylon sleeves on their arms for six hours.
Then mosquitoes were given a choice between two people's sleeves.
One volunteer scored over a hundred times more attractive than the least attractive ones. And for years, the same people kept winning.
The difference was on their skin: more of the acids made from skin oil.
Even mosquitoes bred without key smell sensors could still pick out the magnets.
And blood type? The evidence for it is mixed.
So mosquitoes don't choose sweet blood. They follow the smell of acids made from the oil on your skin.
So who in your family gets bitten the most?
